summary.short: Interim final rule amending the Export Administration Regulations, effective 16 January 2025, for front-end fabricators and OSAT companies exporting advanced logic ICs under ECCN 3A090.a. Adds a worldwide license requirement, a presumption rebuttable through approved IC designer or OSAT lists or attestations, quarterly reporting, and a KYC form.
summary.long: Interim final rule amending the Export Administration Regulations, effective 16 January 2025; compliance with revised text from 31 January 2025. Front-end fabricators and OSAT companies exporting applicable advanced logic ICs under ECCN 3A090.a need a license for any destination worldwide, and such ICs are presumed to be 3A090.a items designed or marketed for datacenters. The presumption can be overcome through an approved or authorized IC designer, a front-end fabricator attestation on aggregated approximated transistor count, or an approved OSAT attestation. Supplements no. 6 and 7 to part 740 list named approved IC designers and approved OSAT companies. License Exceptions AIA and ACM cover 3A090.a items only when designed by an approved or authorized designer. Section 743.9 requires front-end fabricators to file quarterly reports to BIS, first due 31 May 2025, with a KYC vetting form (supplement no. 2 to part 743). Section 748.16 sets an advisory-opinion process for list changes. The rule adds definitions in §772.1, revises the advanced-node DRAM definition, amends the December 2024 FDP IFR, and extends its comment period to 14 March 2025.

notes: Coded from the regulatory text (Part 734-774 amendments and supplements). The preamble is context only. Internal inconsistencies: (1) First front-end fabricator report: section 743.9(c)(1) covers January 15, 2025 to April 30, 2025, while preamble section III.C says January 31 to April 30, 2025; the DATES compliance date is January 31, 2025. (2) Report deadlines: preamble section III.C gives fixed due dates (e.g., May 31, August 31, November 30, February 28), while section 743.9(c)(2)(ii) says each report is due no later than 30 days after the end of the reporting period. Intel and IBM appear in both approved lists and are listed once. Not coded: Executive Order and Federal Register citations in authority lines, OMB control numbers in the Paperwork Reduction Act section, and the unnamed Entity List additions. Obligations, thresholds and events are outside this annotation scope (Tier A sections not requested).

obligations.summary: Front-end fabricators producing ECCN 3A090.a ICs for authorized IC designers must submit quarterly reports to BIS containing the 743.9(b) information (designer name, address and contact, KYC vetting form, product names, model numbers and quantities sold); first report due May 31, 2025, later reports due 30 days after each reporting period ends.
obligations.conditional_on: Sales of ECCN 3A090.a ICs to an authorized IC designer that is not an approved IC designer

evidence.quote: must submit reports to BIS in accordance with this section

obligations.summary: Authorized IC designers must complete the KYC vetting questionnaire in Supplement No. 2 to Part 743 as part of the reporting requirements in § 743.9.
obligations.conditional_on: Designer is an authorized IC designer under Note 1 to ECCN 3A090.a

evidence.provision: Supp. No. 2 to Part 743

obligations.summary: Requests to be added to the approved IC designer or approved OSAT lists must include the Supplement No. 4 information; requests for removal are required when legal status changes, and modification requests when control or name changes; material or substantive changes must be reported promptly to the ERC. OSAT companies are subject to the same request duties.
obligations.conditional_on: Listing request, modification or removal under supplement no. 6 or 7 to part 740

evidence.quote: Any material or substantive change relating to the request must be promptly reported to the ERC, whether approved or still under consideration.

obligations.summary: Only entities that have designed, assembled, tested or packaged ICs, or have credible plans to do so, will be considered for addition to the approved IC designer or approved OSAT lists; entities headquartered in Macau or Country Group D:5 are not eligible.
obligations.conditional_on: Request for addition to supplement no. 6 or 7 to part 740

evidence.quote: Only entities not headquartered or having an ultimate parent headquartered in Macau

obligations.summary: Front-end fabricators and OSAT companies exporting applicable advanced logic ICs are presumed to be dealing with 3A090.a items designed or marketed for datacenters and must comply with 3A090.a requirements unless the presumption is overcome by approved or authorized designer status, a packaging attestation (transistor-count limits) or processing by an approved OSAT; reliance on end-user attestation alone is not sufficient.

obligations.summary: Before April 13, 2026, all IC designers headquartered in Taiwan or Country Group A:1 or A:5 (and not linked to Macau or Country Group D:5) are authorized IC designers if they agree to submit the information in § 743.9(b) to the front-end fabricator.
obligations.conditional_on: Designer not headquartered or ultimately owned from Macau or Country Group D:5; agreement to submit § 743.9(b) information

obligations.summary: From April 13, 2026, an IC designer is an authorized IC designer only if it meets the earlier criteria and has applied to become an approved IC designer; such status lapses 180 days after the application is submitted.
obligations.conditional_on: Designer has submitted an application to become an approved IC designer

evidence.provision: ECCN 3A090, Note 1, a.(3)
